newsitem.title: FRANCE: CGE holds '96 3 bln Ffr property provision.
newsitem.headline: CGE holds '96 3 bln Ffr property provision.

text.p: French utilities company Cie Generale des Eaux reiterated on Monday it would set aside three billion francs for property provisions in its 1996 accounts, as stated last October by chairman Jean-Marie Messier.

A Generale des Eaux spokesman said a news agency report today of a five billion franc provision was incorrect and the company was holding to its plan to provision three billion to cover property losses for the next three years.
Generale des Eaux shares were down 0.27 percent at 744 francs at 1117 GMT, while the market was down 1.24 percent.

The company said in a November letter to shareholders it would make "additional provisions at the end of 1996 to cover the worst-case scenario risks of large-scale property development operations for the next three financial years.
"The resulting exceptional expense will be approximatly FF3 billion," the letter said.
Messier has forecast the 1996 operating profit should exceed the 4.7 billion francs posted for 1994 and the 1996 net attributable gain would be around 1.8 billion.
Generale des Eaux made a 1995 net attributable loss of 3.69 billion francs, due mainly to a collapse in the property market.
